transcript:
Header:
- Date: 2026-03-31
- Time: 15:00 UTC
- Duration: ~55 minutes
- Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Carlos Mendez (CTO, NexGenPay), Aisha Khan (ML Engineer), Samir Patel (Infra)

Auto-summary (auto-gen may be imperfect): staging replay shows throughput gains w/ continuous batching and KV caching; need longer canary to validate tail.

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call?
[00:08] Carlos: Carlos here.
[00:09] Aisha: Aisha on the line.
[00:11] Samir: Samir, yep.
[00:13] Priya: Priya from Redwood. Jordan here too.
[00:16] Jordan: cool, agenda — quick review of last week's run, deep into continuous batching and concurrency numbers, then decide canary window and action items.
[00:28] Carlos: sounds good — we ran the traffic replay overnight, about 2 hours at 50 RPS average, spikes to 140. skipping for time, the sheet is in the shared drive.
[00:40] Priya: saw that — thanks Carlos. quick note: we focused on model variants you gave us, mainly an open 16B variant, token lengths median ~120, p95 ~960. we applied prefix KV caching and continuous batching with a batching window of 15ms to start.
[01:02] Aisha: question — that 15ms window, is that per-request or global across the worker?
[01:08] Priya: it's per serving thread's batching loop; continuous batching accumulates inflight requests and flushes based on either window or certain queue thresholds. so effective batch sizes varied 4-12 depending on concurrency.
[01:23] Samir: we saw CPU spikes on the orchestrator side — might be due to many small grpc connections, could be our network layer.
[01:31] Jordan: noted, Samir. on the numbers: in staging we observed roughly 1.9x throughput at the same cost when enabling continuous batching + KV cache vs baseline (no batching). p95 latency moved from 380ms to ~520ms at higher concurrency levels — tail went up, which is expected.
[01:57] Carlos: 520ms p95 is acceptable for some flows but worried about tail for payment-critical flows. can we target p99 < 800ms?
[02:07] Priya: yes, p99 target is feasible with additional tuning: set concurrency cap per worker, tune queue depth, and enable small-req favoring policy, plus enable adaptive batching thresholds. also can use a preferred model variant for low-latency fast-path (quantized 8-bit).
[02:28] Aisha: how much throughput drop if we pin to the quantized variant?
[02:33] Priya: rough numbers — quantized gives you 20-30% more throughput per GPU but may slightly change output distribution. in your benchmarks, quantization gave us ~2.4x throughput improvements at median token lengths with a minor uptick in short-context hallucination rate we need to validate against eval prompts.
[02:55] Jordan: also tradeoff of hosted vs dedicated — dedicated gives more predictable concurrency limits, and easier to set node-level caps. pricing-wise we'll send delta.
[03:08] Samir: on infra we need to confirm egress and VPC peering. current staging was on a shared subnet, so noisy neighbors may have influenced tail.
[03:18] Carlos: right. we'll try the canary in the isolated VPC next week.
[03:23] Priya: recommended canary: 1 hour replay at 120 target concurrency, 3-minute warmup, observe p50/p95/p99 and GPU util. we'll collect token-level cost and per-route latency.
[03:38] Aisha: can we run a 1-hour longer replay? last time was only 20 minutes at peak.
[03:44] Priya: yes, we ask for 1 hour to capture tails. we also recommend enabling KV prefix cache to catch repeated user prompts; in your dataset ~30% of sessions have common prefixes, so caching helps.
[03:58] Carlos: ok, what about queueing? queue depth was 64 last run — is that optimal?
[04:04] Priya: queue depth of 64 was conservative. with continuous batching you can reduce queue dwell if you tune window and concurrency. recommended starting point for your workload: batch window 12-20ms, queue depth 48, concurrency cap per worker 8-10. this hit our target throughput without blowing p99.
[04:27] Samir: concurrency per worker meaning number of simultaneous generation threads?
[04:31] Priya: yes, number of inflight requests a worker will accept before queueing is applied upstream.
[04:36] Jordan: we measured effective tokens/s per GPU — at concurrency target 120 across cluster we saw average GPU util ~72% and tokens/s ~68k for your model suite. baseline was ~28k tokens/s.
[04:53] Aisha: that's a big jump. need to validate output quality when using quantization and the smaller batch windows.
[04:59] Priya: agreed, we'll run an eval against your prompt set as part of the canary and flag any regression.
[05:07] Carlos: any issues with SMs or kernel selection? last call someone mentioned redwood compiling kernels per model and sometimes picks suboptimal kernels.
[05:16] Priya: yeah, the compilation step will pick kernels based on sequence lengths and hardware; occasionally on first run the warmup compile causes extra latency. we mitigate with ahead-of-time warmups and pinned kernel caches. note: sometimes our auto-detect misreads model name when transcribed, so docs may say 'red wood runtime' — ignore that.
[05:34] Jordan: action item — Priya will share a recommended runbook: warmup sequence, tokens distribution to prime kernels, and quantization checklist.
[05:45] Aisha: quick micro question — do we need to shard model across GPUs for throughput or will single-GPU suffice for our traffic?
[05:52] Priya: depends on model size. for 16B typically single-GPU with NVLink or A100 80GB often OK for your token distribution; if we need horizontal scaling we can shard but then latency and KV cache semantics change.
[06:08] Carlos: let's avoid sharding unless necessary.
[06:11] Jordan: noted. sample numbers from replay: peak concurrency 140 -> observed p95 720ms w/ recommended config; p99 1.1s. baseline p99 was >2.5s.
[06:25] Samir: p99 1.1s maybe borderline for checkout flow — can we route checkout requests to a lower-latency path?
[06:31] Priya: yes — we can set routing policy: low-latency tier uses quantized fast-path model with stricter concurrency caps and shorter batch windows, other traffic goes to cost-optimized pool.
[06:44] Carlos: sounds good. what about caching consistency — do we risk stale context with KV caching?
[06:52] Priya: KV caching is per-session prefix caching, so consistency is fine; it's not a cross-session global cache. eviction is LRU and TTL-configurable.
[07:02] Aisha: any security concerns for KV cache? PII enclosed?
[07:06] Jordan: KV cache in Redwood Dedicated/Private respects customer data policies; we can configure in-flight encryption and no persistence if you prefer. we'll send the security sheet.
[07:16] Carlos: please do.
[07:18] Priya: on queueing we also have adaptive queue sizing — when tail grows we can shrink window to lower batch size, biasing latency. might cost more tokens per second but helps p99.
[07:33] Samir: we need to see memory footprints for quantized models; last time there was OOM on smaller nodes.
[07:40] Priya: we'll include estimated memory per model config. our compile step can also pick a lower-memory kernel.
[07:48] Jordan: timeline: run canary next Wed? Carlos, is that ok?
[07:53] Carlos: yes, Wed works. we need the config by Friday to provision.
[07:58] Priya: we'll deliver config and runbook by Friday.
[08:01] Jordan: any competitors mentioned? Carlos: we did a quick eval of Databricks and Anthropic for latency but they lacked the cost controls we needed.
[08:11] Carlos: also checked AWS SageMaker endpoints but latency jitter was high.
[08:15] Priya: ok noted.
[08:18] Jordan: final recap — Priya to share batching/concurrency recommendations and warmup runbook (due 04-02), Jordan to send pricing delta and security docs (due 04-01), NexGen to run 1-hour canary in isolated VPC (target 04-05) and report back.
[08:36] Aisha: one more question — how to set alerts? We want automatic rollback if p99>1.5s.
[08:42] Priya: we can configure canary monitors in Console: alert on p50/p95/p99 and GPU util; also automatic fallback to a lower-load model variant on breach. we'll send an example policy.
[08:54] Samir: do that.
[08:56] Jordan: great, thanks everyone. we'll follow up in the doc links. meeting adjourned.
